gaps.sentence: 'We'd already booked when you called,' they said. They said they ___ already booked when I called.
gaps.explanation: Past perfect stays past perfect; only the pronoun you → I shifts.

gaps.sentence: She ___ that the storm had passed.
gaps.explanation: Without a personal object, use said (that)...; told requires an object.

gaps.sentence: 'I've been studying all night,' she said. She said she ___ studying all night.
gaps.hint: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
gaps.explanation: have been + -ing backshifts to had been + -ing.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't be late again,' the coach told him. The coach told him ___ late again.
gaps.explanation: Negative commands: not to be, with the negative before the whole infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'It was me who ate the last biscuit,' the boy admitted. The boy ___ eating the last biscuit.
gaps.explanation: Admit takes a gerund (admit doing) or admit that + clause — never admit to do.

gaps.sentence: 'I'm sorry I shouted at you,' he said. He ___ shouting at me.
gaps.explanation: Apologies take apologise for + -ing: apologised for shouting.

gaps.sentence: 'I work from home on Fridays,' he explained. He explained that he ___ from home on Fridays.
gaps.explanation: After a past reporting verb, present simple backshifts to past simple: work → worked.

gaps.sentence: 'Leave now or I'll call the police!' he shouted. He ___ to call the police.
gaps.explanation: A threatening conditional utterance is reported as threatened to do something.
